flagged.evidence: The corollary assumes k>n and says that the increasing-index wedges form a basis indexed by k-element subsets, citing thm-increasing-basis-wedges-form-a-basis. That dependency's Statement is explicitly restricted to "0\le k\le n". It therefore does not license the k>n application used to infer an empty basis.

The definition says "For each degree k" and then declares \star:\Lambda^kV\to\Lambda^{n-k}V, but the exterior algebra is defined only in degrees k\ge0. At k=n+1 the displayed target is \Lambda^{-1}V, which is undefined. The definition needs 0\le k\le n.

To establish two orientations for every \dim V\ge1, the text says that "interchanging two entries of \mathcal B_0 produces a basis with determinant -1." In dimension one an ordered basis has no two entries to interchange. The claim is easily repaired by replacing its sole vector by its negative, but the stated argument fails at that endpoint.

For u=(1,0,1) and v=(0,2,0), \langle u,v\rangle=0, not 1. Thus the displayed Gram matrix \begin{pmatrix}2&1&1\\1&4&2\\1&2&2\end{pmatrix} is not their Gram matrix. The correct matrix is \begin{pmatrix}2&0&1\\0&4&2\\1&2&2\end{pmatrix}, whose determinant is 16; the stated volume \sqrt6 is false (the volume is 4).

Step 1.1 correctly expands \Lambda^2T(e_2\wedge e_3)=6e_1\wedge e_2+2e_1\wedge e_3+e_2\wedge e_3, but then records its coordinate column as (6,6,1) and the displayed matrix has 6 in row e_1\wedge e_3, column e_2\wedge e_3. That entry is 2. Directly, \det A_{13,23}=\det\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}=2, not 6.

The alleged element of V^{\otimes k} is written v\otimes v\otimes e_2\otimes\cdots\otimes e_k. It has 2+(k-1)=k+1 tensor factors (already three factors when k=2), so it is not an element of V^{\otimes k} and cannot be the claimed basis vector there. A valid witness would use e_3,\ldots,e_k after the repeated pair.

This theorem is stated for an arbitrary vector space V. Its proof extends an independent list to "(v_1,\ldots,v_k,u_{k+1},\ldots,u_n)" and invokes thm-increasing-basis-wedges-form-a-basis. The cited dependency is stated only for a finite ordered basis (e_1,\ldots,e_n) and 0\le k\le n; it does not license the infinite-dimensional case of the present theorem.

The Given block permits every k\ge0, while [L4] says increasing-index wedges form a basis and cites thm-increasing-basis-wedges-form-a-basis. That dependency's Statement requires 0\le k\le n. Step 2.1 applies [L4] without imposing k\le n, so it is unlicensed for k>\dim V.

The theorem includes k=0 in its Statement and uses [L5] to construct the determinant coordinate map and assert its value at the identity. But the cited dependency thm-leibniz-determinant-is-alternating-multilinear-and-normalized states "For n\ge1". It does not provide the needed alternating/normalized 0\times0 determinant case.
